title: Introduction to Networks
subtitle: Guess the hidden networking terms — spin for consonants, buy vowels

puzzles.hint: TCP's connection setup ritual: SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK
puzzles.explain: Before TCP can transfer data, the client and server exchange three messages — SYN, SYN-ACK, and ACK — to establish a reliable connection. This process synchronizes sequence numbers and confirms both sides are ready.

puzzles.hint: Burned-in hardware identifier on every network interface
puzzles.explain: A Media Access Control address is a unique 48-bit identifier assigned by the manufacturer to every network interface card. Switches use these addresses to forward frames within a local area network.

puzzles.hint: Lets many devices share one public IP by rewriting packet headers
puzzles.explain: Network Address Translation allows a router to map multiple private IP addresses to a single public IP address, conserving the global address space. It is the reason home networks can place dozens of devices behind one ISP-assigned address.

puzzles.hint: Automatically hands out IP addresses, subnet masks, default gateways, and DNS servers to clients.
puzzles.explain: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol is a network service that automatically assigns IP configuration parameters to client devices when they join a network. Without it, administrators would need to manually configure each device's address, mask, gateway, and DNS server.

puzzles.hint: The physical component that connects a computer to the network
puzzles.explain: The Network Interface Card (NIC) is the hardware that connects a device to a network; every NIC is assigned a unique Media Access Control (MAC) address by its manufacturer, which identifies it on the local network.

puzzles.hint: The human-readable name you see when scanning for Wi-Fi networks
puzzles.explain: A Service Set Identifier is the name broadcasted by a wireless access point to identify a particular wireless network. Client devices display this name in their list of available networks so users can choose which one to join.

puzzles.hint: The most common copper Ethernet cable type found in offices
puzzles.explain: Unshielded Twisted Pair cable consists of pairs of copper wires twisted together to reduce electromagnetic interference, without an outer metallic shield. It is the dominant medium for wired Ethernet in homes and offices and is defined under the TIA/EIA cabling standards.

puzzles.hint: Command-line tool that maps every hop between you and a destination
puzzles.explain: Traceroute is a diagnostic utility that sends packets with incrementally increasing time-to-live values to reveal each router hop on the path to a destination. Network administrators use it to pinpoint where delays or failures occur between two endpoints.
